added_findings.title: CrossSection__SceneData per-scene entries differ between the apps; TD06 is not met
added_findings.detail: The two apps share only the block keys (__Description, __Version, __Scenes). VV's 41 SceneData stores each scene as CrossSection__SceneBinding__{SceneId, UpdatedIso, GizmosVisible, SliceDepthM, FillColor, LineColor, LineWidthPx, Sections[CrossSection__Section__{Name, Mode, NormalXyz, PositionMm, Enabled, GizmoVisible}]} and reads back only that form; all 5 VV project.json files carrying the block use it. TV's 41 SceneData stores the raw Serialize() snapshot {gizmosVisible, sliceDepthM, fillColor, lineColor, lineWidthPx, sections[{name, mode, normalXyz, positionMm, enabled, gizmoVisible}], sceneId}, and Apply reads only that. TV plan s3.2 documented VV's IN-MEMORY snapshot (VV SystemLogic Na__CrossSection__SerializeSections, camelCase) as VV's stored schema. Each app reads the other's entries as an empty sections array, i.e. 'no cuts'. No TV repository file carries the block (0/8), so no shared data is broken today. The S12 report (b.1 item 10, F32, F46, module table) repeated 'byte-compatible'.
added_findings.recommendation: VV: keep its own 41 SceneData writer and reader (DIV-2), and never port TV 41 Na__SectionCut__SceneData__ or Serialize__ into VV. ProjectData only passes the block through, so F46's registration is unaffected. TV back-port (D-S12-V02): CaptureForScene maps the snapshot to VV's prefixed entry keys, and RestoreForScene reads the prefixed form, falling back to camelCase; correct TV plan s3.2.

added_findings.title: project.json folderId is unreliable: never use it for R2 or disk paths
added_findings.detail: Census of the 155 local WCP/Projects/*/*/project.json files (01-Oct-2026): folderId equals the real year/folder in 91, is missing in 10 (e.g. 2026/44371__Gill) and differs in 54 (e.g. 2025/43822__Napthine stores '43822__Napthine' with no year; 2025/59494__Weeks stores '2025/WK-3007__Weeks', an old name). Report b.4 told the facade to 'prefer GetLoadedProjectData().folderId when set', which would send a third of projects' writes to R2 prefixes the app never reads. Every existing VV client (R2SaveProjectJson, R2AssetUpload, R2DrawingNotes) resolves through Na__AppUtils__NormalizeProjectFolderId(?project) and the master index. Whitecardopedia opens VV with ?project=<folderId> taken from the folder it loaded (WCP 03__AppData/Na__AppData__ProjectLoader.js:519 overwrites the file's value), so the URL token is reliable. NormalizeProjectFolderId still guesses '2026/<code>' when the index has no entry (ProjectLoader.js:350). Corroborates S07a-V05.
added_findings.recommendation: The facade and the ProjectLoader helpers resolve the folder only from the URL token via the master index (LookupIndexEntry), refuse writes when it misses (no '2026/<code>' guess), and never read project.json's folderId. Add a facade test with a stale-folderId fixture. Cleaning the field in the data is Adam's call.
added_findings.evidence: parity/verify_s12_r2/folderid_field.py (91 same / 10 missing / 54 differ); VV 03/Na__AppUtils__ProjectLoader.js:335-351; WCP 61__Feature__PwaAppHelpers/Na__Feature__PwaAppHelpers__ValeVisionLinkRouting__Logic__.js:37-54; WCP 03__AppData/Na__AppData__ProjectLoader.js:508-519; report b.4 pre-verification text

notes:
The survey is strong and mostly accurate: 34 of 50 findings were confirmed exactly as written (all 16 critical/high were checked), the code-level evidence held at almost every cited line, and the critical sync-pipeline findings (F01 recursive basename purge, F02 whole-file project.json upload) are right by code reading. No finding was refuted outright; 16 were corrected.

The corrections that change what the swarm builds:
(1) Report b.4 told the facade to prefer project.json's folderId. That field is missing in 10 and wrong in 54 of 155 files, so following it would write a third of projects to R2 prefixes the app never reads (S12-V02). The facade must use the master index only.
(2) 'CrossSection__SceneData byte-compatible (TD06)' is false at entry level. VV stores prefixed binding entries and TV stores camelCase snapshots; each reads the other's as 'no cuts' (S12-V01). VV is safe if TV's 41 modules are never ported into it.
(3) Assets and Persistence are not verbatim ports: TV's DevGate gate contradicts VV's DevGate PORT NOTE and D24 (WP-S12-09 refuted, WP-S12-V09R added).
(4) The spec lockstep (F25) hard-imports the Statement Writer's pure Lockstep module, which WP-S06b-01 already owns.
(5) VV's own headers, and the drawings Description that VV writes into every project.json, claim the sync never touches editor keys, which is false today.

Smaller fixes: F14's old-worker reasoning; F15's HTML-200 trap applies only outside /api/projects/; two more brand-bearing storage keys; a legacy camera key the W2 guard must allow; the shared bucket; the registrar reads no unsaved-work flag; VV's spec PDF and both apps' title-block Project default never get a name (S12-V03).

Watch: seven slices propose overlapping transport packages with conflicting choices (folder names, probe route, spec transport, S08's folderId pattern refusing three existing projects with spaces). Settle D-S12-V01 before scheduling. Nothing was run; R2 contents, the deployed worker version and Cloudflare limits remain unverified.
